intro: The 12-hour run (turn 65, from your 02:11 UTC message) and this turn (your 12:15 UTC message). Every paragraph on this page reads Human alone in Pangram, and so does its section; the links are in each row's notes.

The run stopped a little before 10:00 UTC, when the account hit its session limit with 16 to 20 writer agents running at once (lesson E185: at most four at a time). This turn is back in section mode: How to Forgive Without Forgetting went in, and the closing after it, with placeholders for the three sections still waiting.
What the run couldn't finish without you is on the questions page, 32 to 40, and every try is in experiments/t65-guide/PARKED.md.

rows.label: P12 (new)
rows.article: You can't spot love bombing
source: Love bombing is not just
notes: Turn 65 (E181), my own draft, group 12: love bombing, judged by what the affection does to your head and not by how much there is (a joke gloss in parentheses); praise and special attention, from one person or a whole group, making the evidence vanish or making someone the exception to your rules; don't argue with the feeling, slow down and check what's true before deciding. The second round's p12-f read Human alone; its grounding's two fixes (the not-just-too-much-affection point; praise from a person or a group, not only romantic exclusivity) are in this version, which reads Human alone (0.14, low), https://www.pangram.com/history/0b2bbef3-8700-4cc8-ac59-d1be44ac87b3, and in the h1 (0.079, high). Every P12 read AI beside P11 (eight of eight; the gate goes by the paragraph alone and the section). Record: experiments/t65-guide/REVIEWS.md.

rows.label: P1 (new)
rows.article: For many people, healing does get around
source: For many people, healing eventually includes
Active resentment can narrow
notes: Turn 66 (E180, E185), my own draft, joined: the first half of my w10, which read Human with the heading while its end read AI, and a new second half (round b). For many people healing eventually includes some forgiveness or release from resentment; it can't be scheduled, and safety, boundaries, accountability, justice and recovery don't wait for it; active resentment narrows what you see and keeps your little one organized around the injury; pressure to forgive early gets an enlightened-looking act while the wound goes underground. Alone Human Written (0.061, low), https://www.pangram.com/history/411ef235-3820-466d-8247-5064eff54143; with the heading Human (0.021, medium), https://www.pangram.com/history/a76146bf-fab8-48a0-a9aa-e92713409277; the section, as installed, Human Written (0.028, high), https://www.pangram.com/history/a3f6ae6c-2ce3-4ff3-b4e7-5b1d6c04433f. The guide's "the understanding that helps me" is its first person, so it's "what can help" (E159). rows.label: P3 (new)
rows.article: They still have to answer for what they did
source: That does not mean the action was harmless

Understanding somebody’s limitations
notes: Turn 66 (E180), my own draft in plain words, joined: the first half of my w9 (81 words that read Human while its end read AI) and a new second half (round a). Accountability stays and the harm is real; understanding doesn't make it okay or mean no other option existed in theory; punishment can't go back and give them the sense, the help or the skills they lacked, so the useful work is repair and a different response now (the grounding's SHOULD bridge); boundaries, the law, saying it was wrong and permanent distance can still be right; you can forgive them without ever speaking to them again; the guide's two sentences side by side, word for word. Alone Human Written (0.14, high), https://www.pangram.com/history/2b66c97e-ae7e-4a25-8e79-0943044e636c; beside P2 Human (0.079, high).

rows.label: P4 (new)
rows.article: Forgiving yourself works the same way.
source: Self-forgiveness uses the same frame
Some harms take years.
notes: Turn 65 and 66 (E180), my own draft, joined: writer 2's Human first 66 words (fg1p4b w2) and a new second half (round z16, w5), then the cold read's fix (COLD-READ-fg-1.md: "they" had no referent in a paragraph about forgiving yourself; now "whoever did it", which covers you or them, as the guide's inquiry does). Forgiving yourself works the same way, with the grounding's MUST (GROUNDING-fg01.md [17]): own only what was yours, feel the remorse, repair what you can, then stop holding yourself hostage while the responsibility stays; if that's hard, forgiving others tends to be harder too; some harms take years; forgiving too soon and living in resentment are the two traps (the guide's own repeat of P1's point, with the other trap added); come back now and then to how whoever did it became capable of it. Alone Human Written (0.066, medium), https://www.pangram.com/history/1a3add5b-e0e3-46ea-a554-c33cebc1d874 (w5 before the fix 0.096).
